summary: Former L-5 cab lookout on Klone Peak, Chelan County, WA, built 1931 and destroyed or removed in 1963; sources do not say what remains on the summit today.

facts.status_note: Cab destroyed or removed in 1963 (sources differ on the word). Sources do not say what remains on the summit today; one undated Willhite photo is captioned as an assortment of little items at the summit.

access.note: Reached on foot by trail. Willhite came in from Maverick Saddle, about 12 hiking miles, and found the trails to the summit gave no trouble. The upper Mad River trails close seasonally to everyone but hikers.

visit.trail_note: Many access points, per Willhite. The upper Mad River trails close seasonally to everyone but hikers in late spring and early summer.

events.note: Built as an L-5 cab at the highest point of Klone Peak
Panorama photos taken there on September 18, 1934
Firelookout.com and Willhite say the cab was destroyed; Firetower.org says removed
Registered October 21, 2012 as US 1411, nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firetower.org says the cab was removed in 1963; Firelookout.com and Willhite say it was destroyed. All agree on the year; the story reports both words.

notes_for_editor: Only four pages and no staffing evidence, so the story has no staffing paragraph. No source explains the undated summit photo caption, so the story quotes it without interpreting it; the Trailforks point of interest could not be fetched (HTTP 403) and was not used. Forest Lookouts also carries a 1950 Coast and Geodetic Survey station description calling it a lookout house; not used. Willhite gives 14+3 feet as a photo height, not used.
